initialUserIntent: Make the IDE operational. Complete the JetBrains-style IDE management for Java (the Java language service core), including making RefactorKit support operational as a product feature, and make pi's functioning inside the IDE operational. This slice opens the first coherent behavior slice: the Java language service as an evidence-based BDD requirement.

approvedChanges.statement: Pi is, in the future, ONE of the usable agents in the IDE, not the sole AI/model authority. Requires ADR; no duplicate REQ-IDE-AI-CHAT.

User authorized RefactorKit as a PRODUCT FEATURE (Java/RefactorKit product-surface in scope within bdd-ts). Java TEST infra (JavaSpec, Maven, JUnit-specific policy, Java datasets) and Java-only RefactorKit rules as the workflow's own refactoring authority remain EXCLUDED per workflow contract.
approvedChanges.evidence: User message: 'ok, autorizzo refactorkit come feature di prodotto' (2026-08-21)

requirement.title: JetBrains-style Java IDE management: operational Java language service
requirement.classification: Story BDD (characterization/evidence-based for already-implemented native behavior) + Spec BDD for pure view-model decisions
requirement.capability: Manage a workspace-scoped Java language service (JDT LS spawned and owned by the Rust backend via apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/java_language/*), exposing lifecycle, document synchronization, and Java intelligence (completion, hover, signature help) to the frontend through provider-neutral ports. The desktop controller (apps/desktop/src/features/java/useJavaLanguageController.ts) wires the service into the editor. This slice classifies and validates the already-implemented behavior with an evidence-based status; it does not introduce new AI authority.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given a Java workspace, the language service lifecycle is managed (status/start/stop/restart/poll-events) through JavaLanguagePort adapters, with honest unavailable when no JDT LS/JDK toolchain is discoverable.
Java documents are synchronized (open/change/save/close) to the language service with versioned full text, and only an editor-accepted ready document receives semantics.
Java intelligence (completion, hover, signature help) is requested through JavaIntelligencePort and rendered in the editor surface, treated as untrusted data, with cancellation support.
The flow follows extract -> delegate -> response with no hidden domain policy; absent toolchain or failed requests report honest unavailable/error, never fabricated success.
Boundary invariant: packages/ui, packages/web-core, apps/web never import @tauri-apps/api; browser/Tauri Java implementations live behind frontend ports.

Status is evidence-based with an explicit state (@implemented-and-validated | @implemented-not-e2e-validated | @partial | ...), never inferred from shells; live Tauri-window Java E2E may remain unvalidated if headless (recorded honestly).

requirement.owner: bdd-ts-gherkin-writer (feature) + ts-story-driven (Story) + ts-spec-driven (view-model Spec) + frontend-core-coder/frontend-ui-coder + browser/tauri-adapter-coder + tauri-rust-coder (backend)
requirement.scope: Java language service management and Java intelligence surface (completion/hover/signature) wired in the desktop editor. Classification + validation of already-implemented native behavior. RefactorKit Java refactoring (rename/move/change-signature/safe-delete), Java navigation (definition/references), Java build/run/debug, and project model are SEPARATE later slices, not in this one.
exclusions: JavaSpec, Maven, JUnit-specific policy, Java datasets as workflow test infra
Java-only RefactorKit rules as the workflow's own refactoring authority
RefactorKit Java refactoring operations, Java navigation, Java build/run/debug, project model (later slices)
openQuestions: Characterization RED: since java_language.rs is already implemented, the slice uses characterization scenarios (prove current behavior) rather than new-behavior RED; confirm this is acceptable.
Toolchain: whether a real JDT LS/JDK is expected to be discovered in this environment, or the slice validates the honest-unavailable path plus harness/unit evidence for the spawn path.
Editor wiring: whether Java intelligence must be proven wired into the live Monaco editor or a desktop-harness renderer is acceptable evidence.
Slice boundary: confirm Java language service first, with RefactorKit refactoring/navigation as follow-on slices.
